claims.text: [the user's claim 6, abstract] Power sums of these hashes form a linear set sketch that needs no canonicalization, with the as-written results that support it: at k = 31 the sketch of k-mers as written recovered the 7,931 differences between Cannbio-2 and its draft exactly (137 KB, one round), where a forward-only polynomial hash in the same sketch saw 398,217,248 differences; at k = 63, hashed from the sequence with no packed code, it recovered all 21,382 differences in 549 KB and one round, matching KMC element by element. The k = 63 run used a numpy prototype whose hashes match the C code on 20,000 sampled k-mers, with buckets sized from the true difference. Refuted if 'needs no canonicalization' overstates what was shown (e.g. if canonical k-mers or a canonical truth set enter anywhere in the pipeline the claim credits to S), if the forward-only control is not a fair control, if the k = 63 run did not test what is claimed, if any number fails to reproduce, or if 'linear' is false of the sketch as implemented.
